title: unify terraform private state layout + gpu node pools / iam / networking migration
author: Aisha Gupta
release_notes: Consolidates Private deployment Terraform state layout and unifies GPU node pool, IAM, and networking modules. Provides migration tooling and upgrade path. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Motivation: Our private deployment Terraform modules have drifted across repos and releases which makes upgrades brittle for customers using GPU node pools and custom networking. This PR unifies the state layout for Private deployments, extracts and standardizes GPU node pool, IAM, and networking modules, and provides a migration plan and automated state-move helpers to reduce customer upgrade friction.

What this PR does: - Introduces a unified state layout for private deployments (state/<customer>/<env>/...) and updates module references across the redwood-terraform repo. - Refactors existing gpu_node_pool, private_network, and iam_bindings modules to expose explicit state keys and stable resource addresses. - Adds a migration helper script (scripts/tfstate-migrate.sh) that performs a validated terraform state mv sequence with a dry-run mode and roll-back instructions. - Adds an optional migration flag to the private-installer module (var.auto_migrate_state) that controls whether the installer attempts an automated state migration during upgrades. - Adds comprehensive docs and examples in examples/private-migration/ showing the recommended approach for small, medium, and large deployments. - Adds tests in ./test/integration that run plan/apply against a local backend (GCS minio shim) to validate the new layout.

Backward compatibility & migration: The refactor maintains the original resource names where possible; the state layout changes are additive and non-destructive. The migration helper runs terraform state mv commands in a validated order and supports a --dry-run mode to preview changes. For customers who cannot run the helper, we included a manual migration checklist in examples/private-migration/MIGRATION.md. We intentionally gate the automated migration behind var.auto_migrate_state=false by default to avoid surprises.

Testing & validation performed: - Ran full CI (lint, fmt, validate, unit-tests) across modules. - Integration smoke tests using local backend passed on a simulated 3-node GPU cluster (see CI job infra/integration-gpu: passed). - Performed an internal test migration of a staging private deployment (staging-redwood-2026) and validated that the control plane came back without data loss. - Ran upgrade/rollback rehearsals using the new scripts and documented the observed timings.

Rollout & rollback plan: - Merge to main after approvals. - Cut a patch release for redwood-terraform and notify on #infra-private. - Encourage customers to try the migration in staging using the provided helper and to keep auto_migrate_state=false until they are ready. - If a migration causes issues, the helper supports a reverse state mv sequence and we have a documented rollback checklist (examples/private-migration/ROLLBACK.md).

Notes: This change touches state layout and has operational impact for private customers; please review the migration steps carefully. Related Linear: ENG-5821 (private deploy migration), ENG-5890 (gpu nodepool refactor).

review_comments: Diego Márquez: Please verify that the new state keys do not conflict with existing addresses in older deployments. The migration script should include a deliberate pause between moves for large state objects.

Aisha Gupta (author): Added a validation pass in tfstate-migrate.sh that compares existing addresses and aborts on collisions. Also added a --pause-seconds flag and documentation about tuning for large states.
Priya Patel: Can we make auto_migrate_state default to false in the module input docs? We need to avoid silent migrations during minor upgrades.
Aisha Gupta (author): Done — var.auto_migrate_state defaults to false and examples show how to opt-in. Updated README and examples to reflect this.
Evan Liu: CI flake on the integration job flagged a timing issue when state was >100MB. Suggest split move ordering for large objects.
Aisha Gupta (author): Implemented chunked-move logic and added --chunk-size bytes option; added a note in MIGRATION.md about best-effort retries. Re-ran the integration job and CI passed.
